steps.title: Ordinary chord numbers
steps.body:
**Nashville number system** means writing chord roots as ordinary scale numbers, such as 1, 4 and 5. In the plain major-key pattern, 2, 3 and 6 are minor, and 7 is diminished. A written m can make a minor chord explicit, as in 6m.

**Why it matters:** A band can use the same numbers when it changes the key.

steps.title: See it on the fretboard
steps.body: In G major, 1 is G, 4 is C, 5 is D and 6 is Em. These are the same chords as I, IV, V and vi.

items.prompt: Play G, B and D together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Explore the sounds
steps.body: Write G, D, Em, C as numbers in G: 1, 5, 6, 4. Keep the key name beside the numbers.
